uncited: This method constructs a Linear Bounding Volume Hierarchy (LBVH) acceleration structure specifically for sparse volumetric data to enable efficient empty-space skipping during ray marching.
*   **Output:** An LBVH data structure where nodes contain bounding volumes enclosing the non-empty bricks in their subtree.
Each brick is either empty or contains voxel data.
*   **Bounding Volume:** A bounding box enclosing a set of bricks.
In the context of adapting triangle LBVH, the "geometry" consists of the boundaries of the non-empty bricks.
**Identify Non-Empty Bricks:** Determine which bricks contain data.
This step is performed on the GPU to achieve interactive frame rates.
*   **Brick Size:** Fixed size for the uniform grid partitioning.
*   **Empty Volumes:** If all bricks are empty, the LBVH construction may result in an empty or trivial structure.
Zellmann et al. [ZHL19] proposed this adaptation of a linear bounding volume hierarchy (LBVH) construction algorithm for triangle geometry to sparse volumetric data.
They used the boundaries of non-empty bricks as bounding geometry.
